title: Psalm 23: The Shepherd in the Shadow—An Expository Sermon for Dealing with Terminal Illness
theme: When terminal illness brings us into the valley of the shadow of death, the Lord is not absent; He is our Shepherd, Provider, Restorer, Companion, Host, and Eternal Home.
proposition: The Lord shepherds His people through every stage of suffering and death, sustaining them with His presence and eternal hope.
sermonQuestion: Whose are we when illness and death bring us into the valley?

outline.heading: The Shepherd Gives Personal Assurance When Life Feels Out of Control — “The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.”
The Shepherd Gives Rest When the Body and Soul Are Exhausted — “He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.”
The Shepherd Restores the Soul When Illness Wounds More Than the Body — “He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.”
The Shepherd Gives Courage in the Valley of Death — “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me.”
The Shepherd Comforts and Guides With His Rod and Staff — “Thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.”
The Shepherd Prepares a Table in the Presence of Enemies — “Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies.”

The Shepherd Gives Anointing, Overflow, and Eternal Hope — “Thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever.”

legacyImport.contentPreservation: Original Josh Hetrick legacy sermon preserved unchanged.
